### policy_self_consistency (this task only)

Charter-global conclusions are **cited, not restated**:
`env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/car_rental_desk/_difficulty.md` §§ `policy_conflict_scan`,
`rule_compute_equivalence`, `action_binding_and_uuids`, `prerequisite_graph`, `prerequisite_sentences`,
`override_declarations`, `factor_ladders`.

**Handling time.** Two writes, each evaluated on the world that holds at its own step.

- `frozen_time` = `2026-09-24 10:15:00 MDT`. The rental
  `drive_rentals/064ac9e1-6b66-43f5-b222-53ddb1c40f63` already stands at `status: "cancelled"` with
  `cancelled_at: "2026-09-23 19:40:00 MDT"`. The cancellation itself is **not** a write of this task —
  it happened last night in the app, exactly as the persona says ("She gave the car up in the Wanderlane
  app last night, saw the booking flip to cancelled").
- Step 1 (the prerequisite problem, `drive_ext_cancellation_charge`) is computed on `initial_state`
  alone. Every input it reads — `settled_in_advance_total`, `items_settled_total`, `cancelled_at`,
  `pickup_at`, `booked_date`, the club tier — is seeded. Nothing it reads is produced by a later write.
- Step 2 (the root problem, `drive_ext_cancellation_refund`) is computed on
  `initial_state` **+ step 1's real DB effect**. Its `withheld_on_ledger` binding reads exactly the row
  step 1 creates. Computed early — i.e. on the opening world — it would read 0.00 and give a different
  figure (recorded under `task_independent_derivation` as the contrasting number). The order is forced,
  not chosen.

No formula of either step is evaluated on a world later than its own step; no persona line and no tool
fallback stands in for an eligibility judgement.

**No real-world waits.** Every fact either write consumes is an authoritative record already in
`initial_state` (the rental row, its five ledger rows, the club membership), the real DB effect of the
preceding gold write of this same task (`withheld_on_ledger`), or a choice the customer states
immediately (her consent to the charge coming out of the money already paid). Nothing waits on a
diagnosis, a delivery, a payment clearing, a manual or external approval, third-party processing, a
back-office batch, a future date or a cooling-off period. The refund's *settlement* takes
`refund_processing_days: 14`, but that is the bank's time after the payout is raised, not a precondition
of raising it — base `drive_refund_settlement` raises the payout and then counts the processing days.
The persona is consistent: she asks "how long it usually takes to land" **after** being told the money
has been raised.

**Charter-global defects that bear on this task, demonstrated against this world.**

**F-1 (`_difficulty.md` § findings) — consequence on task 0.**

The renter holds `club_memberships/e5a2e01d-…` — `variant_name: "Wanderlane Platinum"`,
`status: "active"`. `products/club.yaml` gives Platinum `agency_service_fee_waiver: true` and
`car_rental_discount_pct: 8`. The rate class is `Pay Now Standard Rate`, whose
`agency_service_fee_usd` is `12.95`, and `settled_in_advance_total` is `439.83 > 0`. So the extended
policy's **first** `service_element` tier fires: `retained_service_element = 0.0` — the agency service
fee is returned.

Base `drive_cancellation` says, of the very same money: *"the agency service fee is not returned on any
class."* Honouring that inherited sentence gives `retained_service_element = 12.95`.

Recomputed on this world, everything else unchanged:

| reading | `retained_service_element` | scored payout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| extended as written | `0.00` | **`341.04`** |
| base sentence honoured | `12.95` | **`328.09`** |

Two defensible figures for the one scored payout, and `drive_ext_cancellation_refund.overwrite` is `[]`,
so nothing in the charter tells a reader which clause yields. The base sentence is also not a dead letter
on this rental: the extended *charge* policy subtracts `P('agency_service_fee_usd')` from the basis "so
that the share acts on the rate alone", which presupposes the fee sits inside the `439.83` that was
settled in advance. `SOURCE-POLICY RED`.

---

**F-3 (`_difficulty.md` § findings) — consequence on task 0.**

`Pay Now Standard Rate` carries `free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup: 0`.

- Under the rule's own anchor (`confirmed_at` + 0 elapsed hours): the free window closes at
  `2026-08-28 16:40:00 MDT`. The cancellation at `2026-09-23 19:40` is outside it, so a charge is
  withheld — `cancellation_charge_usd = 111.20`, `refund_amount_usd = 341.04`.
- Under the `parameter_schema` gloss ("Hours before collection"): the free window closes 0 hours before
  collection, i.e. at `pickup_at = 2026-10-07 08:00:00 MDT`. The cancellation is **inside** it, and base
  says *"Inside the free-cancellation term nothing is withheld on any rate class and the prepayment is
  returned in full."* — `cancellation_charge_usd = 0.00`, and with `withheld_applied = 0.00` and
  `goodwill_put_back = 0.00 × 25 % = 0.00`, `refund_amount_usd = 424.44`.

Two readings, four figures. The extended charge policy never mentions the free-cancellation term at all,
so it offers no tie-break. `SOURCE-POLICY RED`.

### problem_chain

Walked out from the root problem using the policy and the world alone.

**Root problem.** What the customer brings is: *"what she wants to know is what comes back to that card
and to have it actually set moving today"*. That is money returned to the original form of payment on a
cancelled rental — `drive_ext_cancellation_refund` (`computes: refund_amount_usd`,
`target_tool: post_cancellation_refund_344e0f66`, `owner="agent"`). No other extended policy computes a
return of money.

**Its prerequisite sentences.** `drive_ext_cancellation_refund.rule` opens with exactly one sentence
that joins its own result to something it waits on:

> *"The amount returned to the card that paid is worked out only after the rental's ledger carries the
> charge withheld for the rental being given up."*

**Does that state hold at `frozen_time`?** No. The waited-on state is a cancellation charge standing on
**this** rental's ledger. Scanning `initial_state.drive_rental_entries` for
`drive_rental_id = "064ac9e1-6b66-43f5-b222-53ddb1c40f63"`:

| row | `event_type` | `charge_category` | `amount_usd` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `738d4229-…` | `drive_prepay_charge` | `prepayment` | `439.83` |
| `8b6db416-…` | `drive_extras_charge` | `child_seat` | `83.94` |
| `62d80f88-…` | `drive_extras_charge` | `gps_unit` | `77.94` |
| `659040c6-…` | `drive_supplier_notice` | `""` | `0.00` |

**No `cancellation_fee` line.** `withheld_on_ledger = SUM(… charge_category='cancellation_fee')` over
this rental = **`0.00`**. The prerequisite is genuinely unmet at the opening.

*Near-miss on this very edge.* `drive_rental_entries/f1476b82-…` **is** a `cancellation_fee` line for
`50.00` — but it hangs on the renter's **other** rental, `19677e13-…` (`RA6650184`, Calgary, closed
2025-11-20). A reader who sums the customer's cancellation charges rather than the rental's would find
`50.00` and conclude the prerequisite is already met. The rule's "on that rental" and the DSL's scoping
of `SUM` to the target holding both exclude it.

**Which write brings that state about?** Reading the other policies' own rules as the reader must:
`drive_ext_cancellation_charge.rule` opens *"When a renter gives up a rental, the charge withheld is
worked out on the money already settled in advance on that rental and on the notice the supplier was
given, and is withheld from that money rather than billed separately."* That is the only policy of this
charter whose result is a charge withheld when a rental is given up; its `target_tool` is
`confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472`, `owner="user"`. One reading only.

**Does that problem have prerequisites of its own?** `drive_ext_cancellation_charge.prerequisite: []`,
and its `rule` contains no sentence joining its result to a waited-on state or action with an ordering
connective. Every input it needs is already in the world. The walk terminates.

**The tree the auditor derived:**

```
drive_ext_cancellation_refund   (root, agent, post_cancellation_refund_344e0f66)
        │  value_input  — gate: withheld_on_ledger
        ▼
drive_ext_cancellation_charge   (leaf, USER, confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472)
```

- nodes: 2 — one root problem, **one** prerequisite problem (n = 1, within the 1–3 band)
- edges: 1, `kind: value_input`. Required floor is `max(n−1, 1) = 1` `value_input` edge → **met**.
- cycles: none.
- topological order: `drive_ext_cancellation_charge` → `drive_ext_cancellation_refund`.

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skip the prerequisite write, replay everything else unchanged:
`withheld_on_ledger` stays `0.00` → `withheld_applied = 0.00` (the "vehicle was never collected" tier
reads the ledger) → `goodwill_put_back = 0.00 × 25 % = 0.00` → result =
`RND(MN(MX(424.43595 − 0.00 − 0.00 + 0.00 − 0.00, 0.0), 439.83), 2)` = **`424.44`**, against `341.04`
with the write in place. A swing of `83.40`. **The edge bears weight.**

**Parallel edges.** None — the tree has a single edge, so there is no shared balance, cap or dedup key
for two orders to fight over, and the terminal state is unique.

**No-wait argument.** The resolving action is a single `ctx.create` the renter performs in the
conversation. The persona hands it over on the agent's direction: *"when the agent hands the confirmation
over to her and asks her to put it through herself, she does it there and then and reads back whatever
the system tells her."* No real-world event intervenes.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472` (task_tools.py:12–63)
computes `rid = ctx.make_id(...)`, `amount = round(float(cancellation_charge_usd), 2)`, then one
`ctx.create("drive_rental_entries", rid, …)` and returns a sentence. There is no conditional, no read of
another row, no raise. `post_cancellation_refund_344e0f66` (task_tools.py:66–113) is the same shape.
Neither refuses a call, errors or hints while the prerequisite is unresolved.

**A customer's own write is in the tree.** `confirm_cancellation_charge_358c6472` carries
`@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, and the persona executes it passively at the agent's hand-over
(quoted above) and also consents to the mechanism if asked: *"Should the agent ask her to confirm that
she is content for the charge to come out of the money she already paid rather than be billed separately,
she says yes."* ✓

**The customer raises only the root problem.** `user_scenario` is explicit: *"She does not know, and never
raises, anything about what the terms keep back when a rental is given up."* She names no prerequisite,
asks no "do I need to sort something out first?", and reacts only after the agent explains. She also
issues no second item of work — no document to send, no address, no statement — and closes where the work
closes: *"Once the agent tells her the money has been raised back to the card, she asks only how long it
usually takes to land and, whatever she is told, thanks them and rings off."* ✓

### task_independent_derivation

**Need, authorisation, timing.** She wants money returned to the card she paid with, on the rental she
gave up last night, **today** ("to have it actually set moving today rather than left sitting"), and she
authorises the desk to act for her ("She is happy for the desk to do whatever it has to do on its side"),
while the one write that is hers she performs herself when handed over. She expressly does **not** want
the cancellation reversed, does **not** want a rebooking, and her one hard preference is the form:
*"whatever comes back goes to the card she paid with; she has no interest in credit, a voucher or a
future booking."* That matches `refund_form: "original_payment"` on the rental and base
`drive_refund_settlement`'s "settles to the original form of payment and in no other form".

**Act now / wait / refuse: ACT NOW.** Base `drive_refund_settlement.rental_settled` requires the rental to
stand at cancelled, no-show or returned — it stands at `cancelled` ✓. Nothing in the charter defers the
payout to a future condition, and nothing refuses it.

**Object.** The narrowest business object is rental `064ac9e1-6b66-43f5-b222-53ddb1c40f63`
(`RA7431902`, `HRTZ`, standard, `DENC1`, `2026-10-07` → `2026-10-13`), correlated by
`drive_rental_id`. The renter's other rental `19677e13-…` is excluded: it is `closed`, its dates are
2025, and the persona identifies the Denver October booking. The source ledger line both writes point at
is `738d4229-…`, the single `drive_prepay_charge` of `439.83`.

**Reachability.** `find_customers(full_name="Anneke Vorster")` → the profile; `verify_traveller_identity`
with two of {mobile 7040318294, DOB 1987-03-14, passport_last4 4472} — the persona supplies all three in
order. `find_drive_rentals(customer_id=…)` → both rentals; `find_drive_rental_entries(drive_rental_id=…)`
→ the five rows including the prepayment id the tools need; `find_club_memberships(customer_id=…)` →
Platinum/active. Every policy input is reachable; nothing is hidden in the seed only.

the charge withheld"*. The `withheld_applied` tier the world selects ("the vehicle was never collected",

371.87`. Rental status is unchanged at `cancelled` — neither tool touches it, and no policy of this
difficulty claims a transition.

the factor's own `baseline` binding and replays everything else unchanged.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notice_band` | parameter | ✓ a percentage | "fourteen or more whole days" | `DAYS(cancelled_at, pickup_at) = 14`, exactly on the boundary | `drive_rentals/064ac9e1-…` `.cancelled_at`, `.pickup_at` | 80 % ("the share … is eighty per cent") | ✓ `K('notice_near_pct')` | `264.79` | **✓** |
| `charge_basis_measure` | **method** | ✓ changes which rows compose the basis | "settled in advance **and** optional items paid in advance" | prepay `439.83` > 0 **and** extras `161.88` > 0 | `738d4229-…`; `8b6db416-…`, `62d80f88-…` | the whole of the money settled in advance | ✓ `settled_in_advance_total` | `144.98` | **✓** |
| `member_relief` | parameter | ✓ a percentage | "discount ≥ relief threshold **and** settled ≥ relief settlement figure" | Platinum ⇒ 8 % ≥ 5 %, and `439.83 ≥ 300` | `club_memberships/e5a2e01d-…` (`Wanderlane Platinum`, `active`) **+** `738d4229-…` | no relief | ✓ `0.0` | `115.65` | **✓** |
| `value_band` | parameter | ✓ a multiple | "more than the mid value figure per charged day" | `439.83 / 6 = 73.305 > 60`, not > 90 | `738d4229-…` **+** `.rental_days = 6` | multiple of one | ✓ `1.0` | `108.76` | **✓** |

Baseline check: `baseline.rule` alone — 80 % of the whole `439.83`, no relief, multiple one, nothing for

figure**. `baseline.params: [notice_near_pct]` names the one default key the baseline rule states. Each
factor's fall-through tier equals that baseline value. **No dishonest baseline.**

| `optional_items_kept` | parameter | ✓ a dollar figure | "sold on the day the rental was booked **and** the vehicle was never collected" | extras `posted_date = 2026-08-28` = `booked_date`; `picked_up_at = ""` | `8b6db416-…`, `62d80f88-…` **+** `.booked_date`, `.picked_up_at` | `items_settled_total = 161.88` | `179.16` | **✓** |

Baseline check: `baseline.rule` alone — whole of what was collected (`439.83`), withheld = the whole of
the money settled in advance (`439.83`), retain `12.95`, nothing put back, items kept in full (`161.88`)
→ `439.83 − 439.83 − 12.95 + 0 − 161.88 = −174.83`, floored at `0.00`. **Definite, and different from
gold.** *(Observation: a floored `0.00` is a weak baseline — it teaches the reader only that the answer
is not zero, because `withholding_measure`'s fall-through cancels the whole settlement. It satisfies the
requirement as written; recorded for the record, not as a red light.)*

**Near-miss records present in this world.**

- *Computation A:* `drive_rental_entries/f1476b82-…` — a `cancellation_fee` of `50.00` in the renter's own
  name, on her **other** rental. A careless reader counts it as the charge already standing and stops.
  Excluded by `drive_ext_cancellation_charge`'s "on that rental" and by the DSL's scoping of `SUM` to the
  target holding. Also `c66d8690-…`, an `agency_service_fee` extras line of `9.95` — on the other rental,
  which would otherwise mislead on both `items_settled_total` and the fee to subtract.
- *Computation B:* `drive_rental_entries/659040c6-…` — a real `drive_supplier_notice` with
  `reason_code: "rate_correction"`. It **counts** for `supplier_messages` (giving the 25 % goodwill) but
  **not** for `unavailability_notices`, which filters `reason_code='supplier_unavailable'`. A reader who
  treats "a supplier notice" as "the supplier cannot provide the vehicle" takes the first
  `withholding_measure` tier and withholds nothing. Excluded by the rule's *"a notice … **that the
  supplier cannot provide the vehicle**"*.

**No stamp names the outcome.** No field of `drive_rentals`, `drive_rental_entries` or `club_memberships`
in this world carries a band, tier, share, multiple or relief label. Every tier is reached from a history
aggregate (`SUM`/`COUNT`/`MAX`/`LATEST` over the ledger), a date span (`DAYS`) or a cross-category
parameter (`CPARAM('club', …)`).

**Cross-difficulty evidence is seeded.** `club_memberships/e5a2e01d-b7a3-421f-8773-2216c811a2ec` stands
in `initial_state` for this customer, `status: "active"`, `variant_name: "Wanderlane Platinum"` — a tier
`products/club.yaml` actually defines, with `car_rental_discount_pct: 8` and
`agency_service_fee_waiver: true`. The seeded row does not contradict the club charter. See
`_difficulty.md` O-4 on `club` being a category rather than one of the five difficulties.

**Counts against the bounds.** Computation A: 5 factors (4 `parameter`, 1 `method`) ✓. Computation B:
5 factors (3 `parameter`, 2 `method`) ✓. Over the task: **5 multi-source** factors
(`charge_basis_measure`, `member_relief`, `service_element`, `supplier_message_goodwill` tier 1,
`optional_items_kept`) ≥ 1 ✓; **2 `cross_difficulty`** factors (`member_relief`, `service_element`,
both `club`) ≥ 1 ✓. All ten factors survive the weight tests.

## findings

---

**Finding 0-1 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` (charter-global F-1; consequence demonstrated here).**

- **Verdict.** RED.
- **Symptom.** On this world the scored payout has two defensible values, `341.04` and `328.09`,
  depending on whether the inherited base sentence about the agency service fee is honoured.
- **Root cause.** `drive_ext_cancellation_refund` overrides a base sentence of `drive_cancellation`
  without declaring it: `overwrite: []`.
- **Evidence.** base `drive_cancellation.rule`: *"… the agency service fee is not returned on any
  class."* — extended `drive_ext_cancellation_refund.rule`: *"Where the renter holds an active club
  membership whose tier carries the waiver of the agency service fee and money has been settled in
  advance on the rental nothing is retained …"* — `compute.retained_service_element` —
  `initial_state.club_memberships.e5a2e01d-b7a3-421f-8773-2216c811a2ec.variant_name` = `"Wanderlane
  Platinum"` with `status: "active"`; `products/club.yaml` Platinum `agency_service_fee_waiver: true`;
  `products/drive.yaml` `Pay Now Standard Rate.agency_service_fee_usd: 12.95`.
- **Demonstrated consequence.** Recomputed on this world: `retained_service_element = 0.00` → payout
  `341.04`; `retained_service_element = 12.95` → payout `328.09`. Both readings rest on a sentence in
  force in the merged policy, and the KB renders base and extended together.
- **Affected artifact and location.** `env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/tasks/car_rental_desk/drive.extended.yaml`
  — `extended_policies[1] drive_ext_cancellation_refund.overwrite` (empty), `.rule` (the service-element
  sentences), `.compute.retained_service_element`, `.factors[service_element]`; and
  `policies[drive_cancellation].rule`. Scored solution affected: `evaluation_criteria[8]`'s
  `refund_amount_usd`.
- **Relation to previous revisions.** First revision; no prior audit exists for this difficulty.

---

**Finding 0-2 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` (charter-global F-3; consequence demonstrated here).**

- **Verdict.** RED.
- **Symptom.** The free-cancellation term can be read from confirmation forwards or from collection
  backwards. On this world the two readings put the cancellation on opposite sides of the free window,
  giving `(111.20, 341.04)` or `(0.00, 424.44)` for the two scored parameters.
- **Root cause.** `parameter_schema.free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup` declares a meaning the rule
  that consumes the parameter does not implement, and no `overwrite` or note reconciles them.
- **Evidence.** `drive.extended.yaml:parameter_schema`: *"free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup: Hours
  **before collection** by which a cancellation carries no charge."* vs
  `policies[drive_cancellation].rule` / `.eligibility[inside_free_cancellation].temporal_basis`
  (`anchor_source: drive_rentals.confirmed_at`, `unit: elapsed_hours`). World:
  `Pay Now Standard Rate.free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup: 0`;
  `drive_rentals/064ac9e1-….confirmed_at = "2026-08-28 16:40:00 MDT"`,
  `.cancelled_at = "2026-09-23 19:40:00 MDT"`, `.pickup_at = "2026-10-07 08:00:00 MDT"`.
- **Demonstrated consequence.** Under the gloss, base's *"Inside the free-cancellation term nothing is
  withheld on any rate class and the prepayment is returned in full"* applies and the charge is `0.00`;
  the payout then recomputes to `424.44`. Under the rule's anchor the figures are `111.20` and `341.04`.
- **Affected artifact and location.** `drive.extended.yaml` —
  `parameter_schema.free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup` against
  `policies[drive_cancellation].rule` and `.eligibility[inside_free_cancellation].temporal_basis`.
  Scored solution affected: both writes of this task.
- **Relation to previous revisions.** First revision.

---

**Finding 0-3 — observation. The refund policy's baseline collapses to zero on this world.**

`drive_ext_cancellation_refund.baseline` sets `withheld_applied` to the whole of the money settled in
advance, so the baseline-alone figure is `439.83 − 439.83 − 12.95 + 0 − 161.88 = −174.83`, floored to
`0.00`. It is definite and it differs from gold, so the requirement is met as written; but a reader who
finds only the computation document learns that the answer is "not zero" rather than a substantive wrong
number, and `withholding_measure` alone carries the whole computation. No consequence on any scored
value. (`_difficulty.md` § `factor_ladders` records the structure; this is the per-world note.)

---

**Finding 0-4 — observation. The "optional items" term is subtracted from a base that never contained
them.** `settled_in_advance_total` filters `event_type='drive_prepay_charge'`, so it is `439.83` and
excludes the two `drive_extras_charge` rows (`161.88`). The rule nevertheless says *"the money taken for
optional items paid for in advance is kept in full"* and subtracts `items_kept` from that same base, and
`drive_ext_cancellation_charge`'s basis subtracts `items_settled_total` from it "so that the share acts
on the rate alone" — both of which presuppose the item money sits inside it. On this world the tier taken
is "none of it is kept", so `items_kept = 0.00` and the number is unaffected; but "none of it is kept"
also returns the renter none of the `161.88`, so the rule's promise is not delivered by the formula. No
demonstrable consequence on the scored value here; it would bite on a world taking the fall-through tier
(where the refund would be reduced by money the base never held). Recorded, not red-lighted.

---

**Finding 0-5 — observation (charter-global F-4, checked on this world and inert).**
`goodwill_put_back`'s second branch is `supplier_messages >= 1` where the rule says "one message". This
rental carries exactly one `drive_supplier_notice` (`659040c6-…`), so rule and compute select the same
value (`27.80`) and no second reading arises. Recorded so the charter finding is traceable to this task.

---

**Finding 0-6 — observation (charter-global F-5, checked on this world and inert).** Base
`drive_refund_settlement` requires several payouts on a rental with several lines and caps a payout at
the amount *that line* collected; the extended raises one net payout capped at the **sum** of prepayment
lines. This rental has exactly one prepayment line (`439.83`), so the two caps coincide and
`341.04 ≤ 439.83` satisfies both. Notable only because GT's own
`argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_entry_id` quotes that very base sentence as its authority for
choosing the single source line.

---

**Finding 0-7 — no finding on the derivation.** The auditor's independent derivation reproduced GT
exactly: both scored parameters, both tool identities, both owners, the order, all eight write arguments,
the terminal ledger, the whole problem tree, both whole-baseline figures and all ten factor-sensitivity
figures — every one derived from the policy, the world and the tool contracts alone, before the reveal.
No arithmetic, wording or structural discrepancy was found between the frozen derivation and GT.

### revision-1 reds re-tested on this world

**0-1 / F-1 — CLOSED.** The contradiction revision 1 demonstrated was between base
`drive_cancellation`'s *"the agency service fee is not returned on any class"* and the extended waiver
tier, with `overwrite: []`. `drive_ext_cancellation_refund.overwrite` now carries that exact clause as
`superseded_clause`, verbatim, replaced by the club-waiver sentences (verified in `_difficulty.md` §
`revision_2 / override_declarations`). On this world the extended tier still fires — Platinum,
`agency_service_fee_waiver: true`, `settled_in_advance_total 439.83 > 0`, so
`retained_service_element = 0.00` and the payout is `341.04`. The alternative revision 1 demonstrated,
`retained_service_element = 12.95` → `328.09`, is **no longer defensible**: the base clause that grounded
it is now declared superseded by name, so a reader has one reading, not two. Red closed on its merits,
not by rewording.

**0-2 / F-3 — CLOSED as a red.** Revision 1 demonstrated that
`parameter_schema.free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup` ("Hours before collection") and
`drive_cancellation`'s confirmed-at anchor put this cancellation on opposite sides of the free window,
giving `(0.00, 424.44)` against `(111.20, 341.04)`. The extended charge rule now carries: *"The
free-cancellation term of the rate class booked runs in whole elapsed hours from the moment the supplier
confirmed the renter's booking, **and not backwards from the scheduled collection moment**; a rental given
up inside that term has nothing withheld, and the charge worked out here is the one that arises outside
it."* That names the erroneous reading and rejects it in terms. On this world the term is `0` hours from
`confirmed_at 2026-08-28 16:40`, the rental was given up `2026-09-23 19:40`, so it falls outside on the
only reading the rule now permits, and the charge of `111.20` follows. A reader can no longer reach
`0.00` without preferring a parameter gloss over a normative sentence that explicitly disowns it. The red
is closed.

*Residual, and reported rather than waved through:* the gloss itself is **unchanged and still literally
false** — `parameter_schema.free_cancellation_hours_before_pickup` still reads *"Hours before collection
by which a cancellation carries no charge."* The charter now contains a statement of a parameter's
meaning that its own rule contradicts, and the KB will render both. It no longer produces a second
defensible number, so it is an observation, not a red. The two residual divergences of the new sentence
from base — the clock basis (`frozen_time` vs "given up") and base's dropped *"and the prepayment is
returned in full"* limb — are set out in `_difficulty.md` § `revision_2 / findings` **R2-O-2**; both were
tested on this world and neither produces a second figure, because the term is `0` hours here and both
readings land outside it.

**0-5 / F-4 — CLOSED, checked here.** `goodwill_put_back`'s second branch is now `supplier_messages == 1`,
matching the rule's "one message". This rental carries exactly one notice, so the value is `27.80` either
way, as revision 1 recorded; the divergent world is simply no longer reachable in the compute.

**0-6 / F-5 — CLOSED, checked here.** Both base sentences are now named in `overwrite`. The payout is
still one lump against `738d4229-…`; the un-superseded limb *"the sum of a rental's payouts may never
exceed its ledger total"* is inherited and satisfied (`341.04 ≤ 601.71`).

**0-4 — CLOSED on its merits; what the fix collides with is R2-O-3.** Revision 1 observed that the
formula subtracts optional-item money from a base that never contained it. The new definitional sentence
— *"The money settled in advance on a rental is the total of the advance payments taken on it, and it
carries what was paid for the rental days, what was paid for any optional items bought in advance and the
rate class's agency service fee"* — is **arithmetically true of this seed**, which I verified rather than
took on trust: `Pay Now Standard Rate` over `2026-10-07`→`2026-10-13` is four weekdays at `46.75` plus
Saturday and Sunday at `39.00` = `265.00`; `265.00 + 83.94 + 77.94 + 12.95 = 439.83`, the prepayment

## findings (revision 2)

---

**Finding 0-8 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED`. The cross-difficulty evidence added to this task decides nothing:
deleting the whole `care_policies` table leaves both scored values identical.**

- **Verdict.** RED. New in revision 2; it did not exist in round 1, and it arises from the attempt to
  close revision 1's O-4.
- **Symptom.** `supplier_message_goodwill` now declares `cross_difficulty: care` and this task's world was
  given a `care_policies` row and a gold read node to match. The row is invisible to the binding that is
  supposed to read it.
- **Root cause.** The seeded policy is `status: "expired"`, and the binding is
  `protection_in_force: EXISTS('care', status='in_force')`. `EXISTS` filters the holding table by that
  status, so the row is never matched and the read returns `False` — the identical `False` an empty
  `care` table returns. The tier is therefore carried entirely by `supplier_messages == 1`, a fact of this
  category's own ledger.
- **Evidence.** Ablations run with the harness's own evaluator, everything else replayed unchanged:

  | world | `cancellation_charge_usd` | `refund_amount_usd` |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | as seeded | `111.20` | `341.04` |
  | `care_policies` removed entirely | `111.20` | **`341.04` — identical** |
  | `club_memberships` removed | `115.65` | `328.09` |
  | seeded care policy set to `in_force` | `111.20` | `313.24` |

  `initial_state.care_policies.7ef9d876-935d-4ca4-8c6d-6fb0f4b98794.status` = `"expired"`;
  `drive.extended.yaml:extended_policies[1].compute.protection_in_force`.
  The club rows move both figures; the care row moves neither.
- **Demonstrated consequence.** The scored solution cannot distinguish an agent that performed
  `evaluation_criteria[5]`'s `find_care_policies` read from one that never touched the `care` product.
  This task therefore still has no factor whose tier is decided by another **difficulty's** seeded
  records — its other two `cross_difficulty` factors, `member_relief` and `service_element`, both read
  `club`, which `blueprint.yaml:difficulties` gives no difficulty of its own. That is precisely what
  revision 1's O-4 recorded, so the item is answered rather than closed.
- **Stated fairly.** The expired policy is a genuine **near-miss**: an agent that reads the care table and
  skips the status filter takes the fall-through tier and scores `313.24`. That is real value. It is not
  the same requirement, and it cannot substitute for the one still missing. The author's own
  `design_rationale` concedes the ablation result — *"Remove it and the tier still holds but the evidence
  the agent must read to establish it is gone"* — resting the claim on agent diligence, which no scoring
  can observe.
- **Reviewer hinge.** Under `check_extended.py`'s definition of `cross_difficulty` ("another **category's**
  holding or ledger") this task already qualified in round 1 via `club` and this is an unclosed
  observation; under the skill's "another **difficulty's** records" it is a red. The demonstration is the
  same either way. Recorded so the label can be weighed rather than taken on trust.
- **Affected artifact and location.**
  `drive.extended.yaml:extended_policies[1] drive_ext_cancellation_refund.factors[supplier_message_goodwill]`
  and `.compute.protection_in_force`; `tasks/0.json:initial_state.care_policies` (the `status` value);
  `tasks/0.json:evaluation_criteria[5]`. No scored value is wrong — the defect is that the task does not
  test what the added factor claims it tests.
- **Relation to previous revisions.** Supersedes nothing; revision 1's O-4 remains open and this is the
  demonstration of why the attempted closure does not reach it.

#### problem_chain

**Derived from the policy and the world alone**, starting from the problem the customer raises.

Root problem — *give the confirmed Denver rental up and know what it costs*. The customer's words:
*"the car she has booked in Denver for the end of the month is no longer any use to her and she wants to give it
up, and … she would like to know what giving it up is going to cost her before anything is done to the booking."*
The only extended policy whose subject is `drive_cancellation_charge` and whose rule describes withholding a charge
when a renter gives up a confirmed rental is `drive_ext_release_charge`.

Reading `drive_ext_release_charge`'s rule, it carries exactly one prerequisite sentence:
> *"The release charge is fixed only after the rental's ledger carries the additional driver charge owed for the
> drivers named on the agreement."*

Does that state hold at `frozen_time`? **No.** Row evidence: of the 41 `drive_rental_entries` rows carrying
`drive_rental_id = 12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82`, the `charge_category` values present are
`agency_service_fee` (1), `collision_damage_waiver` (10), `gps_unit` (10), `child_seat` (10),
`vehicle_licence_fee` (10). **No row carries `charge_category = "additional_driver"`.** Meanwhile the rental
records `additional_drivers_count = 4` and the rate class `Pay At Counter Flex Rate` carries
`additional_driver_included_count = 1`, so drivers beyond the free count are in fact named and the charge is
genuinely owed. The prerequisite is unmet, not an eligibility already satisfied.

*Near-miss on the edge itself*: the customer's **other** rental,
`1f698a91-48bc-4f71-a8be-fb21f58a1dba`, does carry a `charge_category = "additional_driver"` line for 54.00
(posted 2025-11-21). A reader who checks "does this renter have an additional driver charge" rather than "does
**this rental's ledger** carry one" would wrongly find the prerequisite already met. The sentence says *"the
**rental's** ledger"*, which excludes it.

Finding the resolving policy, as the reader must (state form — the sentence names no tool): the only extended
policy whose own rule describes raising that charge is `drive_ext_additional_driver_charge` —
*"The additional driver charge on an agreement is the rate class's additional driver fee for each named driver
beyond the free count carried by the rate class …"* — whose `target_tool` is
`charge_additional_driver_79b211ed`, the only tool in `task_tools.py` that creates a row with
`charge_category="additional_driver"`. Single reading.

Questioning that problem in turn: `drive_ext_additional_driver_charge` carries `prerequisite: []` and its rule
carries no ordering connective joining its result to anything else. The tree terminates.

**Derived tree** (isomorphic to the declared one):

```
drive_ext_release_charge            [root, owner=user, release_rental_booking_4b632ce9]
  └── value_input (gate: chargeable_base)
      drive_ext_additional_driver_charge   [owner=agent, charge_additional_driver_79b211ed]
```

- nodes: 2; prerequisite problems n = 1 (within 1..3);
- `value_input` edges: 1 ≥ max(n − 1, 1) = 1 ✓;
- cycles: none;
- topological order: `drive_ext_additional_driver_charge` → `drive_ext_release_charge`;
- **customer's own write present**: the root is `owner="user"`
  (`@tool(owner="user") def release_rental_booking_4b632ce9`), and the persona hands it over passively —
  *"she does it in person rather than having the agent do it for her, using whatever the agent hands her"* ✓;
- parallel edges: none, so no two orders and no competing terminal state.

**Per-edge load-bearing run.** Skip `charge_additional_driver_79b211ed`, replay the release computation unchanged
on the opening world:

| | `ledger_collected` | `chargeable_base` | `result` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| with the prerequisite write | 665.11 | 655.16 | **103.37** |
| prerequisite write skipped | 562.15 | 552.20 | **77.11** |

The scored value moves by 26.26, and `chargeable_base` moves by exactly 102.96 — the additional-driver line
itself, which is precisely what the edge's `effect` claims (*"the binding the share is taken from is larger by
exactly that line"*). The edge bears weight.

**No-wait argument.** `charge_additional_driver_79b211ed` needs nothing but the rental record, its waiver lines
and the club rows, all seeded; it completes synchronously in the conversation and its row is immediately readable.
No real-world event stands between the two writes.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `charge_additional_driver_79b211ed`'s body is
`ctx.find("drive_rentals", …)` → `round(...)` → `ctx.make_id(...)` → `ctx.create("drive_rental_entries", …)` →
return a confirmation string. `release_rental_booking_4b632ce9`'s body is the same shape plus
`ctx.update("drive_rentals", drive_rental_id, status="cancelled", cancelled_at=ctx.now())`. Neither reads the
other's row, tests any ledger state, raises, or returns a hint. Calling the release first would simply succeed at
a wrong amount — the decision stays with the agent.

#### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** `status = "confirmed"`, and `lifecycle.transitions` carries
`confirmed -> cancelled, by: user`. `pickup_at = 2026-09-27 09:00 CDT` is in the future, so
`drive_cancellation`'s *"A cancellation after the scheduled collection time has passed is not a cancellation but a
no-show"* does not bite. The free-cancellation term ended 2026-09-09 16:41 CDT (confirmation anchor), so the
extended policy's scope sentence applies. No supplier-unavailability notice is in the world, so
*"A cancellation made because the supplier itself cannot provide the vehicle is free on every class"* does not
apply.

**Object.** `drive_rentals[12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82]` — the only `confirmed` rental, at `DENDT`
(Denver), `vehicle_class = "suv"`, `rental_days = 10` from 2026-09-27, `booked_date = 2026-09-06`. Every one of
those matches the caller's own account: *"the hire was for ten days from the twenty-seventh, that it is an SUV,
and that she booked it the same day as the flights"* (the air booking's `booked_date` is also 2026-09-06). The
other rental, `1f698a91…`, is `closed`, at `ORDA3`, `compact`, from 2025 — excluded on every one of those
attributes.

**Authorisation and boundary.** She asks for a quote **before** anything is done to the booking
(*"she would like to know what giving it up is going to cost her before anything is done to the booking"*); she
authorises the agent for the preparatory write without being told what it is
(*"she says that is fine, go ahead, and waits without asking what it is"*); and she performs the release herself
(*"she does it in person rather than having the agent do it for her"*). Owner split — agent for
`charge_additional_driver_79b211ed`, user for `release_rental_booking_4b632ce9` — is uniquely entailed by the
scenario and matches the tools' declared owners. She names no further item of work, and she closes the call as
soon as the release is confirmed.

**Identity.** `find_customers` → `verify_traveller_identity` with K = 2 attributes. Reachable from the persona:
mobile `6302884157`, date of birth `1984-02-11`, passport last four `1673` — all matching
`customers[a5d0081a-03e1-477c-b4a2-771821c68e27]`. She will not read a card number; none is needed.

#### factor_weight

Recomputations below are the auditor's own, on this task's handling-time world.

**Computation 1 — `additional_driver_charge_usd`.** Baseline rule: *"the rate class's additional driver fee for
each named driver beyond the free count carried by the rate class, taken for every booked rental day of the
agreement"* → (4 − 1) drivers × 12.00 × 10 days = **360.00**. Definite, self-sufficient from
`baseline.params = [additional_driver_fee_per_day_usd, additional_driver_included_count]`, every sentence of it
present in the `rule`, and **different from gold (102.96)**. An agent who reads only the computation document
arrives at a definite, wrong answer.

| factor | effect | honest? | tier taken / records | `baseline.rule` value | scored under baseline | bears weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `club_free_driver_allowance` | parameter (2 vs 3 vs class's 1 — a count) | `P('additional_driver_included_count')` = 1, exactly what the baseline rule's "free count carried by the rate class" gives | tier 2: `variant_name = Wanderlane Gold` + `XSUM(qualifying, 12m) = 6800 ≥ 6000` | 1 | **137.28** | **yes** (≠ 102.96) |
| `charged_day_length_basis` | method (three different day formulas) | `booked_days`, exactly the baseline's "every booked rental day" | tier 2: `booked_days = 10` ∈ [7, 13] | 10 days | **121.12** | **yes** |
| `waiver_backed_driver_fee` | parameter (16.00 / 9.50 / class's 12.00) | `P('additional_driver_fee_per_day_usd')` = 12.00, exactly the baseline's "the rate class's additional driver fee" | tier 2: 10 CDW rows ≥ 10 booked days **and** `vehicle_class = suv` ∉ {premium, luxury, van} | 12.00 | **130.05** | **yes** |
| `advance_naming_relief` | parameter (15 / 5 / 0 per cent) | `0`; the baseline rule states no relief | tier 1: `DAYS(booked_date, pickup_at) = 21 ≥ 21` **and** `corporate_program_id = ""` | 0 | **121.12** | **yes** |
| `multi_driver_weighting` | method (weighting vs plain count) | `chargeable_drivers`, exactly the baseline's "for each named driver beyond the free count" | tier 1: 2 chargeable **and** 10 ≥ 7 booked days | 2.0 | **137.28** | **yes** |

Counts: 5 factors (within 4..6), **3 `parameter` + 2 `method`** (≥ 2 and ≥ 1). All five survive. Substituting all
five baselines at once gives **360.00**, a definite number ≠ 102.96.

*Near-miss for this computation*: `club_points_entries[f571dc60…]`, a `qualifying` accrual of **4900 points**
posted **2025-09-02** — exactly twelve months and fifteen days before `frozen_time`, so
`MONTHS(2025-09-02, 2026-09-17) = 12` and the window `0 ≤ m < 12` excludes it. The rule sentence that excludes it:
*"that has accrued at least the middle qualifying threshold of qualifying points **in the last twelve months**"*.
A careless reader sums all four qualifying rows and gets 11700.

*Stamp — D-4 demonstrated here.* `club_memberships[429792c1…].qualifying_points_pts = **6800**`, which is exactly
the figure the rule asks the reader to compute with the twelve-month window. The schema calls that field
*"identically the sum of the qualifying_points account deltas"*, which is 11700, and its own gloss ties it to the
*current qualifying period* (`tier_effective_date = 2026-03-01`), whose sum is 3600. It equals neither; it equals
the rule's rolling-twelve-month aggregate. Consequence: an agent that never reads the points ledger, never applies
the window and never notices the 4900 near-miss reads 6800 off the membership row, lands on the same tier
(`6800 ≥ 6000` → 2 free drivers) and scores the same 102.96. Reading the stamp and reading the rule cannot be told
apart by the score, and the only near-miss this computation has is neutralised at the same time. **SOURCE-FACTOR
RED**, per `_difficulty.md` / `### findings` / D-4.
(Independently: including the 4900 row would still give 11700 ≥ 6000 and the same tier, so the window's exclusion
is not by itself score-distinguishable either.)

`rule`, and **different from gold (103.37)**.

*Cross-difficulty evidence, seeded and checked against its own charter*: `linked_disruption_relief` reads `air`.

*Near-miss for this computation*: the customer's **other** rental,
`drive_rentals[1f698a91-48bc-4f71-a8be-fb21f58a1dba]`, carries a `drive_prepay_charge` of **248.00**, four

*Stamps naming the outcome*: none for this computation. No field on any record names `withheld_share_pct`,
`chargeable_base`, `disruption_relief_pct`, `member_relief_pct` or `returned_items_total`. The one field that
duplicates a computed quantity is `charges_total_usd` — finding D-1 — and it **disagrees** with the rule's value
rather than stamping it, which is why it is a unique-solution defect rather than a stamp.

### findings

**T0-1 — observation (instance of `_difficulty.md` / `### findings` / D-1).**
- *Verdict*: observation. Downgraded from the red this audit initially carried, on the grounds set out below;
  the evidence and both figures stand on record either way.
- *Symptom*: `drive_rentals[12a9dc68…].charges_total_usd = 432.25` while the rental's 41 seeded ledger rows sum to
  **562.15**, and `db_schema.json` declares the field *"identically the sum of the rental_charges account deltas"*.
- *Root cause*: the seed carries a deliberately stale holding total —
  `design_rationale` states outright that the desk must *"read the rental's own ledger rather than the cached total
  on the holding, which is deliberately stale"* — against a schema that words the relation as an identity rather
  than as a cache that may lag.
- *Evidence*: `tasks/0.json` `initial_state.drive_rentals.12a9dc68-8e24-4709-9100-dc0240bccd82.charges_total_usd`;
  `blueprint/db_schema.json` `drive_rentals.charges_total_usd`; `blueprint/products/drive.yaml`
  `binding.quantity_fields`.
- *Demonstrated consequence*: a reader who takes "the money standing on the rental's ledger" from the field the
  schema promises is that sum computes `0.5 × (432.25 + 102.96 − 9.95 − 249.80) × 0.6 × 0.85 = ` **70.24** instead
  of 103.37.
- *Why observation and not red*: the policy surface is unambiguous about which rows it means —
  `compute.chargeable_base` is built from `SUM('drive_rental_entries','amount_usd', …)`, `inputs.history` names
  `table: drive_rental_entries`, and the rule says *"the money standing on the rental's **ledger**"*, the ledger
  being `binding.event_tables = [drive_rental_entries]`. A stale holding total is a cache diagnostic, which this
  audit's own charter excludes from red-lighting. What remains reportable is the schema's wording: "identically"
  states an invariant the seed breaks in all three rentals of this difficulty.
- *Affected artifact*: `tasks/0.json` `initial_state.drive_rentals[*].charges_total_usd`;
  `blueprint/db_schema.json` `drive_rentals.charges_total_usd`.
- *Relation to previous revisions*: first revision.

**T0-2 — observation.** `prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time.evidence` lists
`initial_state.drive_rentals.12a9dc68-…-dc0240bccd82.charges_total_usd` among the three evidence paths for why the
prerequisite is unmet. That field shows nothing about whether an `additional_driver` line stands on the ledger —
the fact the closure's own `why_false` prose correctly rests on is the **absence of such a row in
`drive_rental_entries`**, which is not among the three paths listed. The closure's figures (552.20 → 655.16) are
correct and match this audit's recomputation, so no scored value is affected. Affected artifact: `tasks/0.json`
`prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time.evidence`.

**T0-3 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (instance of `_difficulty.md` / `### findings` / D-4).**
- *Verdict*: SOURCE-FACTOR RED. The tier of `club_free_driver_allowance` is readable off a stamp that agrees with
  it, so reading the stamp and reading the rule cannot be told apart by the score.
- *Symptom*: `club_memberships[429792c1…].qualifying_points_pts = 6800` is **exactly** the figure the rule asks the
  reader to compute — `XSUM(club_points_entries.points_delta, points_kind='qualifying', within_months=12)` = 3200 +
  2100 + 1500 = 6800 — and it sits on the very holding row the ladder's first condition already reads for
  `variant_name`.
- *Root cause*: the seeded value of a summary field was set to the rule's rolling-twelve-month aggregate instead of
  to the quantity the schema defines for it.
- *Evidence*: `blueprint/db_schema.json` `club_memberships.qualifying_points_pts`: *"tier-qualifying points counted
  in the current qualifying period; **identically the sum of the qualifying_points account deltas**"*. On this
  world the sum of all qualifying deltas is **11700** (3200 + 2100 + 1500 + 4900) and the sum over the current
  qualifying period (`tier_effective_date = 2026-03-01`) is **3600**. The seeded 6800 is neither. `design_rationale`
  describes the membership row as *"Wanderlane Gold, active, enrolled 2019-04-12"* and never mentions the field,
  so the collision was not noticed.
- *Demonstrated consequence*: an agent that reads `qualifying_points_pts` off the membership row, never opens
  `club_points_entries`, never applies the *"in the last twelve months"* window and never sees the 4900 near-miss of
  2025-09-02, evaluates `6800 ≥ 6000` → `mid_tier_free_drivers = 2` → **102.96**, the scored value. The window, the
  ledger read and the computation's only near-miss are all bypassed at no cost to the score, so the factor stops
  discriminating between a reader of the rule and a reader of the record. (`find_club_points_entries` is action 5 of
  GT precisely to make that ledger read necessary; on this world it is not.)
- *Affected artifact*: `tasks/0.json`
  `initial_state.club_memberships.429792c1-d19c-4f02-b162-163d3155e324.qualifying_points_pts`, against
  `drive.extended.yaml` `drive_ext_additional_driver_charge.factors[club_free_driver_allowance]` and
  `compute.club_qualifying_12m`; the invariant in `blueprint/db_schema.json`.
- *Relation to previous revisions*: first revision.

**R5-O-4 — observation, new this round (residual of D-1, not a regression).**
On the **seeded** world every summary field now satisfies its declared identity. But the two gold writes add ledger
rows without updating the holding's cached total — no task tool in this framework aggregates a history into a
derived value, and all four here only `ctx.create` a row and `ctx.update` a status — so at the **release's own
handling time** `charges_total_usd` stands at 562.15 while the rental's rows sum to 665.11, a lag of exactly the
102.96 driver line. A reader who took the money the share acts on from the cached field at that moment would get
`0.5 × (562.15 − 9.95 − 249.80) × 0.6 × 0.85 = ` **77.11**, which is also the skip-the-prerequisite answer.
Recorded as an observation and not a red, on the same two grounds revision 4 used to downgrade D-1: the rule says
*"the money standing on the rental's **ledger**"*, `compute_basis` quotes it, and `inputs.history` names
`table: drive_rental_entries`, so the policy surface points at the rows and not at the holding; and a cache
diagnostic is excluded from red-lighting by this audit's charter. It is structural to the framework's tool
contract rather than to this charter, and the worklog states it openly rather than papering over it
(*"the cached total lags the rows by exactly the additional driver line the agent has just raised"*), which is the
right handling. Affected artifact: `task_tools.py` (all four tools) against `blueprint/db_schema.json`
`drive_rentals.charges_total_usd`.

**No regression found on this task.** The rate class, dates, driver count, waiver lines, air booking and both
scored values are unchanged; all ten factors still bear weight against unchanged baselines; the problem tree, its
single `value_input` edge, the `owner=user` root and the no-wait argument are unchanged; all seven gates re-run
green.
